problem: The lead says flatly that HTTP runs on top of TCP. That is true for HTTP/1.0, 1.1 and 2, but HTTP/3 runs over QUIC on UDP, and the 'Beyond' note later says exactly that, so a careful student sees a contradiction.
fix: Say 'HTTP/1.1 runs on top of TCP, so bytes arrive in order and none are lost' and let the HTTP/3 note at the end carry the exception.

problem:
The reply declares Content-Length: 5120 bytes but the body shown is the 18-byte line

Networks

. A student checking the arithmetic will think the header is wrong.
fix: Add a line under the block saying the body is cut short for display, or use Content-Length: 18 to match the one body line shown.

where: Section 1, request line rule (also Exam traps, last point)
problem: 'never the full URL' is stated as absolute. When a request goes to a proxy, the request line carries the absolute URI (GET http://host/path HTTP/1.1); only requests to an origin server carry the path alone.
fix: Keep the rule but add: 'a request sent to a proxy instead carries the absolute URL in the request line'.

problem: Code 500 is given the reason phrase 'Server Error'. The standard reason phrase is 'Internal Server Error'; 'server error' is the name of the 5xx class, not of 500.
fix: Change the 'Means' cell to 'Internal Server Error'.

problem: 'On a slow link this removes several round trips' mixes up bandwidth and delay. Pipelining pays off when the round-trip time is large compared with transmission time; a slow (low-bandwidth) link with a short RTT gains little.
fix: Say 'On a high-latency link this collapses several round trips into one'.

problem: 'the reply carries the same status line the request expects' is misleading: a request contains no status line, only a start line with method, path and version.
fix: Say 'the request carries no status line; the status line appears only in the reply, here 200 OK'.
